subject: MedAxis DPA: hosting footprint clarification and role-routing
messages:

Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai; ben_carter@redwood.ai

Subject: MedAxis DPA: hosting footprint clarification and role-routing

Hi Sara / MedAxis legalOps,

Thanks for sending the initial redline — appreciate the fast turnaround. We reviewed MedAxis_DPA_Redline_v3 and had two cross-cutting questions that affect how we map controller/processor roles and whether a transfer-impact addendum is required: 

1) Hosting footprint: the redline refers to locations in the EU + US + APAC but the hosting-map attachment shows only US and Ireland nodes. Can you confirm whether APAC persistence (e.g., Singapore) is in scope for the contract period? If APAC hosting is planned, we'll need a short transfer-impact addendum and SCCs sequencing.

2) Role split for subprocessing: section 3(c) proposes the customer-delegation model for analytics (MedAxis is controller; Redwood as processor) but they added language that pushes certain routing decisions back to MedAxis ("routing authority"). That is a material change — our legal team can accept a narrow routing approval right for security-critical tiers, but not blanket control.

Attached: a quick hosting map template (medaxis-hosting-map.xlsx) and our redline request tracker. Can you ask your IT team to confirm the node list and whether any PII is retained in APAC?

If helpful, happy to run a 30-min sync tomorrow. Proposed next steps:
- MedAxis IT confirms hosting nodes and retention zones (reply to thread)
- MedAxis legal flags any mandatory wording for distributor/subprocessor routing
- Redwood legal (laura + ben) to provide counter-markup and a short mutual action plan to close within 7 business days

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Head of Contract Strategy, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: MedAxis DPA: hosting footprint clarification and role-routing

Karthik — thanks, and good questions. Quick answers below; attached is our internal hosting-map export (medaxis-hosting-map.xlsx) with notes.

1) APAC: currently we have a short-term pilot in Singapore for latency-sensitive telemetry, but no long-term persistent storage of customer PII there. The master dataset is replicated to Ireland and US for persistence. For the pilot we wrote that APAC nodes "may" process telemetry in memory only; apologies for the ambiguity.

2) Routing authority: our legalOps wants the ability to request routing changes for compliance investigations (e.g., keep specific datasets in Ireland). They are not asking for realtime control of runtime routing, just contractual approval rights over region-based hosting for certain data classes.

We've attached our redline (MedAxis_DPA_Redline_v3.docx) — the relevant clause is 5.2(b). LegalOps would prefer to see a short clause requiring Redwood to implement region routing within 10 business days of a written request.

We'll aim to confirm the APAC persistence question by EOD tomorrow (IT is pulled in).

—Sara
Sara Johnson
Senior Counsel, MedAxis

Attachments: MedAxis_DPA_Redline_v3.docx, medaxis-hosting-map.xlsx
From: laura_bennett@redwood.ai

Cc: sara.johnson@medaxis.com; legalops@medaxis.com; it@medaxis.com
Date: 2026-09-15T08:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MedAxis DPA: hosting footprint clarification and role-routing

Karthik / Ben — internal notes and proposed positions below (short and directive so sales/legal can move fast):

- APAC hosting: if MedAxis confirms "no persistent PII stored in Singapore" we accept a representational statement and will add a conditional transfer-addendum template that only kicks in if persistence changes. This keeps time-to-close down.

- Routing authority: we cannot accept an open-ended contractor obligation to change routing within 10 business days for arbitrary requests — operationally this is risky and could break SLAs. Offer: accept contractual right for MedAxis to issue "region-of-record" requests limited to (i) regulatory orders and (ii) data subject binding legal demands, and require Redwood to respond with a remediation plan within 5 business days and implement within 10 business days where feasible. If implementation requires new capacity/regions, parties will discuss cost/ETA.

- SCCs sequencing: suggest we keep SCCs execution conditional on the mutual action plan. If APAC persists PII, then we add a short transfer-impact addendum referencing the standard EU SCCs and include an evidence handback timeline.

Action items for the thread:
1) Sara / MedAxis IT to confirm persistence status (EOD 9/15).
2) MedAxis legal to confirm whether their "10 business day" ask is mandatory or advisory.
3) Redwood to produce counter-redline with the limited routing solution and a 7-business-day mutual action plan.

I will draft the counter by COB today and upload to the Drive link. Ben — can you confirm if SOC 2 evidence and our KMS whitepaper suffice as initial evidence, or do they want additional encryption attestation?

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Director, Legal — Contracts, Redwood Inference
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai

Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai; ben_carter@redwood.ai; it@medaxis.com

Subject: Re: MedAxis DPA: hosting footprint clarification and role-routing

Sara / team — appreciate the quick confirm. Per Laura's note and the attachments, next steps and timeline: 

1) MedAxis IT confirmed in thread that Singapore will not persist PII (thanks). We'll treat APAC as in-memory processing only; Redwood will include a conditional transfer-impact addendum that activates if persistence changes.

2) Routing language: Redwood can accept a narrow "region-of-record" request path limited to regulatory/legal requirements. We'll provide counter-redline with the following behavior: MedAxis issues written request -> Redwood acknowledges within 3 business days with feasibility assessment -> plan to implement within 10 business days if it requires configuration changes only; if it requires new region provisioning, parties will negotiate cost and ETA.

3) Evidence: Ben, please attach SOC 2 summary + KMS whitepaper to the Drive folder. Also copy to legalOps for initial evidence handback.

4) Proposed meeting: 30 min on Friday 9/17 to walk the counter-redline and confirm action plan. Sara — please confirm availability or propose an alternative.

I'll upload the counter-redline and the mutual action plan to the Drive link this afternoon. If MedAxis is comfortable with the conditional addendum model we'll aim to close DPA redlines within one week.

Thanks everyone — moving to action.
Karthik
Head of Contract Strategy, Redwood Inference
